text:
Bo Horvat had a rough Wednesday against Carolina, and one listicle put him among the most disappointing Islanders. Over a bigger window, the picture is less of a slump than a stall: eight points in his last ten games when we'd expect about ten, despite playing nearly 22 minutes a night, up almost two and a half minutes on his usual load.

The process is fine. He is generating 1.39 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, well above his 1.02 last season, and the Islanders take 53% of the five-on-five chances with him on. His 14.9% shooting is normal, and the team around him is finishing below its chances. Evolving-Hockey made the same point about last season: the chances were there, the goals weren't, and he was doing it against the opponent's best lines (99th percentile competition).

His game is built on the rush. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off it. Our projection puts him near 39 goals, which would be a big year. The minutes say the Islanders believe it.
headline: Horvat is getting chances, not results
